data.meta_description: Do you need a licence to charter a yacht in Marbella in 2031? Updated rules for bareboat & skippered charters. Book your boat in Puerto Banús today.
data.summary: A clear guide to the 2031 licence requirements for chartering a yacht in Marbella, covering bareboat and skippered options, with practical advice for first-timers.
key_facts: Skippered charters require no licence – the skipper holds all certifications.
Bareboat charters need a Spanish Recreational Navigation Licence (PER or equivalent).
The PER licence requires a medical exam, theory test, and practical exam.
EU/EEA licences are valid in Spain; non-EU licences may need an official translation.
Minimum age for a skipper licence in Spain is 18 years old.
All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance.
Puerto Banús is the main departure point for our fleet of 15+ boats.

faq.q: Do I need a licence to charter a yacht in Marbella?
faq.a: No, if you book a skippered charter. Our fleet, from the Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) to the Ferretti 94, includes a licensed skipper who handles all navigation. For bareboat charters, you need a Spanish PER licence or an equivalent foreign licence.

faq.q: What is the Spanish PER licence?
faq.a: The Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo (PER) is the standard Spanish licence for recreational boats up to 15 metres. It requires a medical certificate, a theory exam, and a practical test. You can take courses at Spanish nautical schools.

faq.q: Are foreign licences accepted in Spain?
faq.a: Yes. EU/EEA licences are automatically valid. Non-EU licences (e.g., USCG, RYA) are generally accepted, but you may need an official Spanish translation or a certified copy. Check with the Spanish Directorate General of Merchant Marine before your trip.

faq.q: What is the minimum age to charter a boat in Marbella?
faq.a: For a skippered charter, there is no minimum age – children are welcome aboard. To operate a boat yourself under a bareboat charter, you must be at least 18 and hold a valid licence.

faq.q: Can I charter a boat without any experience?
faq.a: Absolutely. All our charters come with a professional skipper who handles the boat. You just relax, enjoy the views of La Concha, swim at Cala del Faro, or sip cava. No experience or licence needed.

faq.q: What documents do I need to bring for a skippered charter?
faq.a: Just a valid ID or passport for each passenger. No licence or boating experience is required. We handle all paperwork, insurance, and safety checks.

faq.q: Are there any changes to licence requirements in 2031?
faq.a: As of 2031, Spain has not introduced major changes to recreational boating licences. The PER remains the standard. Always verify with the Spanish authorities or your charter company for the latest updates.

faq.q: What happens if I charter a boat without a valid licence?
faq.a: Chartering a boat without a licence can result in fines, confiscation of the vessel, and legal liability. To avoid risks, book a skippered charter with us – we provide the skipper, so you stay compliant and worry-free.

data.body_html:
Planning a yacht charter in Marbella for 2031? One of the first questions that comes up is whether you need a licence. The short answer: if you book a skippered charter with us, you don't need any licence at all. But if you're considering a bareboat charter, the rules are different. This guide covers everything you need to know about Marbella yacht charter licence requirements 2031, from the Spanish PER to foreign licence recognition, so you can get on the water without hassle.

Do you need a licence for a skippered charter?

No. Every boat in our fleet – from the Marbella yacht charter Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) to the Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h) – comes with a licensed skipper included. The skipper holds all necessary certifications, so you and your guests can focus on enjoying the Costa del Sol. You just need a valid ID. This is the simplest way to charter a yacht in Marbella, especially if you're a first-timer or don't hold a boating licence.

Bareboat charter licence requirements

If you want to captain the boat yourself, you need a Spanish Recreational Navigation Licence, commonly called the PER (Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo). This licence allows you to operate boats up to 15 metres in length. To obtain it, you must pass a medical exam, a theory test, and a practical exam. Courses are available at nautical schools across Spain, including in Marbella and Málaga. The minimum age is 18.

Foreign licence recognition in Spain

EU and EEA recreational boating licences are valid in Spanish waters without additional paperwork. For non-EU licences (e.g., USCG, RYA, or ICC), Spain generally recognises them, but you may need an official translation or a certified copy. Always carry your original licence and, if possible, an International Certificate of Competence (ICC). We recommend checking with the Spanish Directorate General of Merchant Marine before your trip to avoid any issues.

What about the 2031 rule changes?

As of 2031, Spain has not introduced major changes to recreational boating licence requirements. The PER remains the standard, and foreign licence recognition rules are stable. However, regulations can evolve, so it's wise to confirm with your charter company or the local port authority in Puerto Banús before your departure. We keep our licence requirements page updated with the latest information.

We offer over 15 boats, all departing from Puerto Banús. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). Here's a quick overview of our most popular options:

On the day of your charter, you'll meet your skipper at the dock in Puerto Banús. After a quick safety briefing, you'll cruise along the Golden Mile, past La Concha, and perhaps stop for a swim at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. The skipper knows the best spots and handles all navigation. You just bring sunscreen, swimwear, and a camera. No paperwork, no stress.

Ready to book? Explore our fleet and choose the boat that suits your group. For any questions about licences or anything else, contact us via WhatsApp – we're happy to help. Whether you're celebrating a birthday, hosting a corporate event, or just enjoying a day at sea, Marbella's coastline is waiting.
